notes: No primary document states 4-5 non-fatal drownings per drowning death. The exact wording was found only in an esanum.com press article (undated, no byline) that introduces it with 'it is estimated', names no source, and lists only the WHO 2024 report, which the lab has already confirmed carries no ratio. The WHO fact sheet (1 May 2026), the WHO 2014 Global report (p. vii: non-fatal data 'not routinely collected'), the WHO health-topic page, and the WHO Europe (2023), SEARO (2021) and EMRO (2025) pages give no ratio either. Recommend retiring row who-nonfatal. The nearest documented ratios are place- and denominator-specific: Australia hospitalisations 2.71 (peer-reviewed), Ontario ED visits 3.6 ('nearly four'), United States children 5 (CDC fact sheet October 2014, seen only as cited by BMJ Open 2015) and 7 (CDC stacks document reviewed 7 October 2022), Alberta 6, New Zealand under-5 hospitalisations 6.9, NSW ambulance 15; a '4-5' figure most plausibly arose by blending the Ontario 'four' and the CDC 'five', but no document says so, and none of these may be presented as global or combined. Row cdc-nonfatal-ed-2012-2021 was checked against the CDC Drowning Facts page (last reviewed 27 January 2026): 8,111 ED visits per year versus 4,083 deaths per year, 2012-2021, consistent with 'about 2 per death'; no correction needed. The 'old' values in corrections are taken from the task brief because the ledger file was not accessible in this run. The proposed grade C for who-nonfatal reflects press provenance under the lab's definitions; keeping D until retirement is equally defensible, since the substantive finding is that no document supports the figure. Several fetches were blocked or failed (listed in tried); the 2014 WHO report was read from an official Spanish Ministry of Health mirror, and the 2008 child injury report and pre-2024 WHO fact-sheet versions remain unverified.
